newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan refuses comment on rebel execution reports.
newsitem.headline: Japan refuses comment on rebel execution reports.

text.p: Japan's foreign minister on Monday denied knowing whether Peruvian forces who stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last week executed unarmed hostage-takers.
"The details of what exactly took place in the operation are not clear, so Japan is not in the position to comment on that," said Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda.
Ikeda, who returned from Peru on Monday, told a news conference he had heard accounts of the raid from hostages and other sources in Lima.

The foreign minister was noncommittal when asked whether he had heard accounts that Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas had been executed, as Japanese media had interpreted remarks he made at a Lima news conference.

"(In Lima) I said the details are not clear, so I will refrain from commenting," Ikeda said. "It is the same now." President Alberto Fujimori has vehemently denied accusations Peruvian commandos executed two unarmed MRTA rebels in Tuesday's raid.

A former hostage, a commando who took part in the raid, military, police and rebel sources have suggested that troops shot to death two rebels they had caught and held in an upper-storey room of the mansion.
All 14 MRTA rebels, two commandos and one hostage, a local judge, died in the dramatic attack which freed 71 hostages who had been held in the residence for 126 days.
